title: Wyoming signs MOU for expedited permitting under FAST-41
summary: Wyoming recently adopted a measure to accelerate federal and state permitting processes for its infrastructure projects, including uranium mining projects. On October 26, Wyoming Gov. Mark Gordon and Emily Domenich, executive director of the Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council (Permitting Council), signed a memorandum of understanding to bring the state’s infrastructure projects in line with the requirements of Title 41 of the Fixing America’s Surface Transportation Act, also known as FAST-41.

title: Fusion companies sign agreements during Japan-Germany meeting
summary: Last week during a visit to Japan, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz met with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. The two leaders issued a joint declaration on advanced technology cooperation, including a commitment to collaborate on stellarator and laser-based fusion energy technologies. Coinciding with the visit and the signing of the bilateral declaration, several German and Japanese fusion organizations announced new agreements to cooperate on various aspects of fusion development and commercialization. According to a joint statement, “The two leaders underscored that collaboration and exchange in the field of advanced technology, including space and fusion energy, is a key pillar of bilateral ties.”

title: Antares, Last Energy, and Radiant hit DOE authorization milestones
summary: The month of October saw three of the original Reactor Pilot Program companies hit a handful of milestones as each pursues Department of Energy authorization for the operation of various reactor projects. Both Last Energy and Radiant earned documented safety analyses (DSAs) for their first reactors, and Antares earned its nuclear safety design agreement (NSDA) for its second reactor.
